matches.rationale: No finding identifies inconsistency between the Figure 6(b) table values and the Figure 6(a) learning curves. Findings 6 and 7 address other data discrepancies (text-vs-table, figure-vs-appendix) but not the table-vs-curves inflation described in the ground truth.

Finding 2 directly identifies the sign error in the advantage weighting of f^{return} in Section 3.1, stating that the negative sign reverses the intended effect, which is exactly the method logic issue described in the ground truth.

Finding 12 identifies that IIF's hyperparameter p is selected per environment by reporting the best, while baselines use fixed untuned hyperparameters, matching the selective hyperparameter disclosure issue in the ground truth.

Finding 1 identifies that the abstract's claim of completely eliminating sample inefficiency and solving training instability is unsupported by the 20-67% reductions shown later, capturing the same claim interpretation distortion.

The ground truth concerns potentially fabricated or premature citations (Cheng/Deng 2025). Finding 4 points to a different missing reference (Kumar et al. 2024) and does not address the cited works in the ground truth.
No finding mentions the omission of ethical considerations, failure modes, or societal impact in the RLHF toxicity mitigation experiments, which is the core of this ground truth item.

No finding explicitly identifies the marketing-style language and rhetorical exaggeration in the introduction (e.g., 'first study,' 'revolutionary breakthrough'). Finding 1 addresses factual overstatement in the abstract, which is a distinct rhetorical issue.

Finding 3 identifies the contradiction between a fixed pre-trained reference policy and a dynamic evolving reference in the same section, matching the cross-section incoherence about π^{ref} described in the ground truth.
Finding 11 identifies the explicit statement about optimized axis ranges and omission of early Acrobot rounds in the Figure 6 caption, matching the visual encoding manipulation ground truth exactly.

Finding 12 identifies the unfair tuned-vs-untuned comparison where IIF benefits from per-environment hyperparameter optimization while baselines use fixed untuned hyperparameters, matching the experimental design issue in the ground truth.

No finding mentions the wide confidence intervals, the contradiction between 'consistently improves' claims and performance degradation in Highway round 9, or the cherry-picking of favorable interpretations.

Finding 5 identifies the inconsistent use of θ_j^{(k)} in the influence equation I_i and the deviation from the TracIn formulation described earlier, matching the method logic consistency issue in the ground truth.
No finding addresses the selective reporting of environments or the suppression of negative results where IIF failed or performed worse than baselines.
No finding identifies the misattribution of f^{return} as structurally equivalent to REINFORCE with a baseline or the inaccurate reference to Sutton and Barto 2018 Section 13.4.

No finding identifies the inconsistency between the main text's claim of 'negligible overhead' and the substantial influence calculation cost (7-15% of total time) revealed in Table 5 of the appendix.
